original_question: Is it true that for every sequence (z_n)_{n>=0} in the d-dimensional unit cube [0,1)^d there exists a constant c_d > 0 such that the discrepancy D_N of the first N points satisfies D_N >= c_d (log N)^d / N for infinitely many N?
target_in_paper: The draft is trying to capture the unnumbered general discrepancy conjecture stated in Section 1 (Introduction) and repeated in Section 4 after Open Problem 16: for every sequence in [0,1)^d, the ordinary discrepancy D_N should satisfy a lower bound of order (log N)^d / N for infinitely many N. It is not Open Problem 17, which is only a special 2-dimensional base-2 digital-sequence case.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely on the main mathematical content: it quantifies over arbitrary sequences (z_n) in [0,1)^d, asks for a constant c_d > 0 depending on the dimension, uses the lower-bound scale (log N)^d / N, and requires the inequality to hold for infinitely many N. This is essentially the same conjectural lower bound stated in the paper.
missing_details: The paper uses the ordinary discrepancy D_N, not the star discrepancy D_N^*; this distinction matters because D_N^* is defined separately just before the conjecture.
To be fully stand-alone, D_N should be defined explicitly by D_N := sup_B |A_N(B)/N - lambda(B)|.
The supremum is over all axis-parallel subintervals B subseteq [0,1)^d, not only boxes anchored at the origin.
A_N(B) should be defined as the counting function A_N(B) := # {0 <= n < N : z_n in B}, so 'the first N points' means indices n = 0,1,...,N-1.
lambda should be identified as d-dimensional Lebesgue measure (volume) on [0,1)^d.
The dimension should be stated as a fixed integer d >= 1.
The constant c_d should be said to depend only on d, not on the sequence or on N.
The paper presents this as a conjecture/open general problem, with the one-dimensional case already known by Schmidt; that contextual status is omitted in the draft.
refined_question: For each fixed integer d >= 1, let (z_n)_{n>=0} be an arbitrary sequence in [0,1)^d, and for N >= 1 define its discrepancy by D_N := sup_B |A_N(B)/N - lambda(B)|, where the supremum runs over all axis-parallel subintervals B subseteq [0,1)^d, A_N(B) := # {0 <= n < N : z_n in B}, and lambda is d-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Is it true that there exists a constant c_d > 0, depending only on d, such that for every sequence (z_n)_{n>=0} one has D_N >= c_d (log N)^d / N for infinitely many positive integers N?
justification: The draft matches the paper's unnumbered conjecture almost verbatim. In the Introduction, immediately after defining the discrepancy D_N and distinguishing it from the star discrepancy D_N^*, Larcher states that 'for every sequence' in [0,1)^d one should have D_N >= c_d (log N)^d / N for infinitely many N. Section 4 repeats the same general conjecture after Open Problem 16 and then specializes to Open Problem 17, which asks only for the 2-dimensional base-2 digital-sequence case. Because your draft ranges over every sequence in [0,1)^d and is not restricted to digital sequences or to d = 2, the correct target is the general unnumbered conjecture, not Open Problem 17.
